SMTO-JOB-0014 — The Gateway has no record of this background job

GUID: 60a88622-93a3-4a78-975c-38b0a8cb40ec
Slug: gateway-job-not-found
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) about a background job, but it has no saved record of it. That doesn't prove the job never ran; it may have run on another Gateway.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which Gateway this conversation is using and make sure it's the computer that started the job. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways to see your Gateways. Each Gateway only keeps records of the jobs it started itself.
  2. Ask the agent to check the job it started earlier in this conversation, describing it in words rather than typing a job reference. A mistyped or old job reference won't match anything the Gateway has saved.
  3. Before asking for the work to run again, check on that computer whether it already happened, for example whether the expected files or changes are there. A missing record doesn't mean the job didn't run, so running it again could repeat the work.

What success looks like

  • The task shows the job's status or output, or you've confirmed whether the work already happened.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't start a replacement job until you know the first one didn't already make its changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GatewayJobs.get/status found no record for the requested job_id on this Gateway (error_kind gateway_job_not_found); a missing record is not proof that the job never ran or that its process exited.

What this means

  • GatewayJobs.get/status finds no retained job record for the requested ID. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • GatewayJobs.get/status finds no retained job record for the requested ID.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the owning Gateway and retained job list before deciding whether history was removed or the wrong target was selected.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the job_id and that the request went to the Gateway node that launched it (compare the node or Gateway identity in the original job receipt). If the record is really gone, check the target system for the job's effects before launching any replacement.
  • Refresh the job list on the owning Gateway and verify the exact job identity. Missing local history does not prove a remote mutation did not occur.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original job is located or its external state is reconciled without assuming missing history means no effect.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
